note: #2767 item 13 (a CRLF body's captured Setext candidate-text line keeps its trailing "\r", defeating the thematic-break exclusion and misreading two ordinary "---" lines as a Setext heading): the comment's own specific mechanism (a false-positive misread of two ordinary thematic breaks) does not reproduce -- under CRLF, NEXT_HEADING_PATTERN's search previously returned no match at all for every construction tried (the underline line's own trailing "\r" blocked the pattern's own line-end alternative), a total false-negative miss rather than a false match (PARTIAL). The consequence was still real and dangerous in the same family: with the boundary never found, the Acceptance Criteria section scan became unbounded and silently absorbed a later, unrelated section's substantive bullet, turning a should-fail placeholder-only AC section into a wrongly-passing one purely because of CRLF line endings. FIXED (#3287, Copilot review on that PR): NEXT_HEADING_PATTERN's Setext branch now uses "\r?\n" for both the content line's own terminator and the underline's own trailing whitespace/terminator, matching the sibling pattern in triage-structural-evidence.mts (NEXT_ATX_HEADING_PATTERN), which already carried an explicit "\r?\n" fix for exactly this class of bug. This entry's own verifiability now correctly rates "fail", the same as an otherwise-identical LF body. Unrelated to item 13's own claim: checkAutonomy (Check 6) also fails on this body, because its own literal "- TBD" placeholder line independently matches the UNRESOLVED_CHOICE_SOURCE pattern -- an artifact of the placeholder text choice, not a #2767 gap.
